title: RC-14 a buy that lands has no database row until its whole submission returns (minutes on a private bundle), and stopping the bot in that window (Ctrl+C runs the cleanup that closes the DB and exits at once) or any crash leaves a held token the bot does not know about; synchronous=NORMAL can also roll back the last commits on a power loss

evidence.note: V2 snipe: await submitBuyTx(...) covers every private attempt and its confirm window; the signed bundle can be included while this await is still pending
only after it returns: recordSnipe, then insertTrade.run (the first and only durable record of the buy)
first SIGINT/SIGTERM: arm the grace timer, then run cleanup() synchronously
cleanup closes the API, timers and providers, calls closeDb() and process.exit(0); an awaiting buy never reaches insertTrade
the comment says abandoned in-flight submits are safe because restart-resume finds them; for a buy there is no row to resume

forceWalCheckpoint is applied only to pause/resume; its comment says a commit can be lost on SIGKILL, which is not how WAL+NORMAL behaves (process death keeps committed frames; power loss or an OS crash can roll them back)
no write-ahead buy intent row and no boot-time check of wallet token balances against trades rows exists at the base SHA

sibling_sites_checked: All three buy row writes (bot.ts:773 deliberate, :1127 V2, :1451 V3) are written after the awaited submit. The catch-path loss of a landed buy is AUD-BUY-002 (RC-01, error path) and is not repeated here; this entry is the process-death path. Process-ending conditions already registered elsewhere that can hit inside the window: AUD-BUY-005 (unhandled rejection exits), AUD-TX-009 (bundle-wait crash), AUD-ANTIRUG-002 (WS reconnect crash). The restart scan (db.ts:597-620, bot.ts:1904-1960) reads only rows that exist. exit_state and lp_baseline are written after the trade row by armPositionMonitoring (BUY slice, SC-06).
severity_rationale: S1 STRAND, equal to the research suggestion, strengthened by the shutdown path: stopping the bot is a routine operator action (the operating notes say to force-kill the process), and the first signal closes the database and exits immediately, so a buy in its multi-minute submission window is lost to the bot even on a clean stop. The token then sits in the wallet with no exit monitor, no anti-rug watch and no dedup record. Not S0 because it needs a stop or crash inside the window. The synchronous=NORMAL part is power-loss only and is recorded as a sub-claim, not proven here.
recommendation: Write a buy intent row (token, chain, nonce, signed hash(es)) before the first submission and reconcile it at boot against the chain (schema 7 to 8); make the first shutdown signal wait for in-flight buys up to the grace period instead of closing the DB at once; decide synchronous=FULL. Card OD-18. Phase 24; nothing is changed in Phase 22.

sub_claims.claim: No durable record of a buy exists between the first signed submission and the end of submitBuyTx
The first shutdown signal closes the DB and exits without waiting for an in-flight buy
synchronous=NORMAL under WAL can roll back the last committed rows after a power loss or OS crash (SQLite documented behaviour; process death alone does not lose them)
No boot reconciliation compares wallet token holdings with trades rows
